lines.text: This opal was once a seashell.
Opalized shells have been found at Lightning Ridge, Australia.
Opal can fill the space left when a fossil dissolves.
Australia's opal fossils are about 100 million years old.
lines.say: Australia's opal fossils are about one hundred million years old.

lines.text: A shallow inland sea once covered central Australia.
Silica rich water filled the voids where shells and bones lay.
Tiny silica spheres in opal break light into rainbow colors.
At Lightning Ridge, opal has even replaced a dinosaur's jaw.
Pinecones have turned to opal there too.
A miner found Eric, an opalized sea reptile, in 1987.

post.caption: This opal was once a seashell. Opalized shells have been found at Lightning Ridge, Australia. Opal can fill the space left when a fossil dissolves, and Australia's opal fossils are about 100 million years old, from when a shallow inland sea covered central Australia. Silica rich water filled the voids where shells and bones lay, and tiny silica spheres in opal break light into rainbow colors. At Lightning Ridge, opal has even replaced a dinosaur's jaw, and pinecones have turned to opal there too. A miner found Eric, an opalized sea reptile, in 1987, and public donations of over $500,000 helped buy Eric.
